q1_issues.issue: "broader" is a comparative, and Comparatives says a comparative does not entail the positive, so the flat (Member … broad) asserts something the sentence does not.
The scale symbol increase (also in statement 4) appears nowhere in the text — "was up 9.05 points" states a change in value, while Measure records an entity's value on a stated dimension.
The scale level and the unit point for "at 972.64" are likewise supplied rather than read off the surface dimension the Measures rule requires.
The parenthetical identifier <.SPX> is left unrepresented.

q2_gaps: attributive comparative with an elided standard ("the broader Index", "the larger firm"): only predicative "X is ADJ-er than Y" with an explicit Y is covered
delta / change-of-value measures ("was up 9.05 points", "fell 3 percent", "gained 2 cents"): Measure has no change form and no licensed scale word for "up" / "down"
"or" as an appositive restatement of one value in another unit ("9.05 points, or 0.94 percent"): the Disjunction section would wrongly make this an opaque (Or …)
a parenthetical ticker / alias alongside a proper name (<.SPX>): exactly one Name atom is licensed and there is no alias or identifier relation
notes: Treating the appositive "or" as two coexisting measures rather than an (Or …) is the right call even though the instruction set does not say so. Name/kind handling of the multi-word index name follows the Kestrel-River pattern correctly.
